> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

`TensorMatcher::with_device<Codes...>(sym)` and `with_dtype<Ts...>(sym)` called `set_options` even with an empty pack, which replaced the symbol's options with an empty list (= anything allowed). The common launcher idiom `device.set_options<kDLCUDA>(); TensorMatcher(...).with_device(device).verify(x);` therefore never checked the device type, so a CPU tensor passed. About 200 of 260 `SymbolicDevice` declarations under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/` used this idiom. The same bug affected the dtype restriction in `distributed/nvlink_comm.cuh`.

Introduced in #14570, which added the `set_options` call to the symbol overloads; before that (#13453) they left the symbol's options untouched, so every launcher written with this idiom since has had an unchecked device type.

## Modifications

- `tensor.h`: `with_device(sym)` / `with_dtype(sym)` only override options when the pack is non-empty. `set_options` now re-checks a value that is already bound, so a runtime `DLDevice` / `DLDataType` passed together with a type list (e.g. `.with_device<kDLGPU>(x.device())`) is checked too; that path was also unchecked before.
- Replace hard-coded `kDLCUDA` / `kDLCUDAHost` with `kDLGPU` / `kDLGPUHost` in JIT launchers and headers (`jit/csrc`, `jit/include`, `kda_kernels/csrc`), so the check is correct on ROCm. `moe/paged_experts.cuh` needed `using sglang::kDLGPU;` because it only imports `sglang::host`.
- Left as `kDLCUDA` because they are CUDA-only and don't include `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`: `jit/csrc/moe/tvm_ffi_utils.h` (`cudaGetDevice` + CUDA stream helper), the vendored `ops/lora/moe/trtllm_lora_temp/data/csrc/trtllm_fused_moe_kernel_launcher.cu`, and the device-name table in `tensor.h`.
- `add-jit-kernel` skill examples updated to `kDLGPU`, plus a note that options set on a symbol stay in force.
- New `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_tensor_matcher.py`: JIT-compiles a small launcher and checks that a CPU tensor or a wrong dtype is rejected through both the symbol path and the runtime-value path. All 4 cases fail on the old header.

## Fallout

No launcher started rejecting its inputs: no test anywhere hit `not in the allowed options`, so no call site or declared option needed changing.

Note: `moe/expert_specialization/es_sm100_mxfp8_blockscaled_{group_quant,moe_group_gemm}.cuh` are not referenced by any JIT loader and already fail to compile on main (`host` is not visible there). They were only touched by the rename.

## Accuracy / tests

- All `test/registered/kernels/ops/**` and `test/registered/unit/kernels/**` on 1x B200. Every failure reproduces on main with identical counts (`paged_mqa_metadata`, `q8kv8_sparse_prefill_backend`, `tilelang_dsa_zero_rope`, `model_fast_paths`, diffusion `test_rope`, `hy4_decode_kernels`, `lanczos`, `moe_topk_softmax`, `per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2`). The rest are multi-GPU or ROCm-only tests that can't run on a single CUDA GPU.
- Multi-GPU communication tests on 4x H200: `all_reduce_residual_norm`, `deterministic_reduce_scatter`, `fp4_allgather_moe_reduction`, `tp_qknorm`, `custom_all_reduce`, `symm_mem_all_gather` pass. `ar_fusion` and `beam_all_reduce` need 8 GPUs (left to CI).
- Every changed header compiled standalone for sm_100a on this branch vs main: no new failures.
- ROCm not run locally; relying on AMD CI.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Hand-written checks that should become matcher expressions (`RuntimeCheck(t.dim() == ...)`, stride / contiguity / alignment checks, raw dtype `.code` / `.bits`, `TVM_FFI_ICHECK`) remain in about 90 files under `jit/csrc`, e.g. `distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh`, `gemm/fp8_blockwise/fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120.cuh`, `elementwise/fused_qknorm_rope.cuh`, `inkling/inkling_all_reduce.cuh`, `deepseek_v4/hash_topk.cuh`.

detail.title: [Fix] TensorMatcher: keep symbol device/dtype options; use kDLGPU aliases

files.patch:
@@ -96,11 +96,11 @@ This is the **primary validation API** for all kernel launchers. Use it to valid
 
 - **`host::SymbolicSize{"name"}`** — A named symbolic dimension. Call `.set_value(n)` to pin it, `.unwrap()` to extract after verification.
 - **`host::SymbolicDType`** — Symbolic dtype. Use `.set_options<Ts...>()` to restrict allowed types.
-- **`host::SymbolicDevice`** — Symbolic device. Use `.set_options<kDLCUDA>()` to restrict to CUDA.
+- **`host::SymbolicDevice`** — Symbolic device. Use `.set_options<kDLGPU>()` to restrict to the GPU (`kDLGPU` / `kDLGPUHost` from `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh` resolve to the CUDA or ROCm device type). Options set on the symbol stay in force when it is later passed to `.with_device(device_sym)` without a type list. Keep `kDLCUDA` only in kernels that cannot build on ROCm (inline PTX, cute/cutlass, flashinfer).
 - **`host::TensorMatcher({dims...})`** — Fluent builder for tensor validation:
   - `.with_dtype<T>()` — require a specific C++ type (e.g. `fp16_t`)
   - `.with_dtype<T1, T2, ...>()` — allow a set of types
-  - `.with_device<kDLCUDA>(device_sym)` — require CUDA and bind the checked device to a `SymbolicDevice`
+  - `.with_device<kDLGPU>(device_sym)` — require the GPU and bind the checked device to a `SymbolicDevice`
   - `.with_strides({strides...})` — validate strides (omit to require contiguous)
   - `.ensure_alignment(bytes)` — require the data pointer **and every stride except the innermost** to be a multiple of `bytes` (a power of two). Size-1 dimensions are skipped, since their strides are arbitrary. This is how a vectorized kernel states its precondition; see the alignment convention above.
   - `.verify(tensor_view)` — execute the check; throws `PanicError` with full context on failure; **chainable** (`verify(a).verify(b)` to check multiple tensors with the same shape)
@@ -110,10 +110,10 @@ This is the **primary validation API** for all kernel launchers. Use it to valid
 ```cpp
 auto N = SymbolicSize{"num_elements"};
 auto device = SymbolicDevice{};
-device.set_options<kDLCUDA>();
+device.set_options<kDLGPU>();
 TensorMatcher({N})  //
     .with_dtype<fp16_t>()
-    .with_device<kDLCUDA>(device)
+    .with_device<kDLGPU>(device)
     .ensure_alignment(16)  // e.g. for 128-bit vectorized load/store
     .verify(dst)
     .verify(src);  // same shape, dtype, device as dst
@@ -122,7 +122,7 @@ const DLDevice dev = device.unwrap();
 const int64_t last_dim = 128;
 TensorMatcher({N, last_dim})  // a fixed dimension can be a plain integer
     .with_dtype<fp16_t>()
-    .with_device<kDLCUDA>(device)
+    .with_device<kDLGPU>(device)
     .verify(tensor_2d);
 ```
 
@@ -361,11 +361,11 @@ void scale(tvm::ffi::TensorView dst, tvm::ffi::TensorView src, float factor) {
   // 1. Validate input tensors with TensorMatcher
   SymbolicSize N = {"num_elements"};
   SymbolicDevice device_;
-  device_.set_options<kDLCUDA>();
+  device_.set_options<kDLGPU>();
 
   TensorMatcher({N})  //
       .with_dtype<T>()
-      .with_device<kDLCUDA>(device_)
+      .with_device<kDLGPU>(device_)
       .verify(dst)
       .verify(src);  // same shape / dtype / device as dst

@@ -273,7 +273,7 @@ auto verify_matvec_inputs(
 
   TensorMatcher({rows, input_size})  //
       .with_dtype<fp16_t, bf16_t>(dtype)
-      .with_device<kDLCUDA>(device)
+      .with_device<kDLGPU>(device)
       .verify(input);
 
   CHECK_HOST(input_size > 0 && input_size % kQuantBlock == 0)
@@ -282,11 +282,11 @@ auto verify_matvec_inputs(
 
   TensorMatcher({slots, cache_bytes})  //
       .with_dtype<uint8_t>()
-      .with_device<kDLCUDA>(device)
+      .with_device<kDLGPU>(device)
       .verify(cache);
   TensorMatcher({records})  //
       .with_dtype<int32_t>()
-      .with_device<kDLCUDA>(device)
+      .with_device<kDLGPU>(device)
       .verify(slot_ids);
 
   CHECK_HOST(records.unwrap() == rows.unwrap() * records_per_input)
